To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
environmental costs are real and measurable, environmental benefits have a value and environmentally friendly transport policies can be economically more efficient than the current policies.

(1) the environment is a public good; (2) the market is a poor mechanism for allocating the costs and benefits of environmental quality; (3) environmental costs are a real economic cost; (4) environmental benefits have real economic values; (5) an environmentally friendly transportation policy is being constructed which is economically more efficient; and (6) the environmental benefits of an efficient transportation system are greater than the environmental costs of an efficient transportation policy.
the environmental benefits of environmentally friendly transport are real economic benefits and that the economic costs of environmentally unfriendly transport are real economic costs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the economic implications of environmental protection in the transport sector?
the question of how to achieve a sustainable transport system in the context of the economic and environmental constraints that exist in the real world of the 1990s.
the following question: Can a transport policy be environmentally friendly, economically efficient, politically feasible and politically acceptable?

environmentally friendly transport is both environmentally and economically beneficial, and therefore should be possible to implement.

the economic and environmental interests of the transport sector are complementary, and that the economic and social benefits of environmentally friendly transport policies are far greater than the costs.

environmental costs are real, that environmental benefits are real, that environmentally friendly transport is more efficient than the alternatives, and that it is possible to find the means to implement environmentally friendly transportation policies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the environmental costs of transport are real economic costs and the environmental benefits have a positive real economic value.
we have been able to demonstrate that environmental costs are real costs and that environmentally friendly transport policies can be economically efficient.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the environmental costs of transportation are substantial and that they can be reduced substantially by the use of new technologies, by the use of pricing mechanisms, by the use and design of new infrastructure, and by the use of regulations.

the environmental and health benefits of a green coalition are significant and that these benefits are likely to be larger in urban areas than in rural areas, and in developing countries than in developed countries.
